jobs.occupation: PostDoc position (m/f/d) in  Data-Driven Social-Ecological Research (Umweltwissenschaftler/in)
jobs.description: Senckenberg Society for Nature Research (SGN), headquartered in Frankfurt am Main, is seeking to fill the following position at the Senckenberg Biodiversity and Climate Research Centre (SBiK-F), starting as soon as possible:PostDoc (m/f/d) in Data-Driven Social Ecological Research(Full-Time / Part-Time** **options available)Location: Frankfurt am MainEmployment scope: Full-Time; Part-Time options are availableType of contract: Temporary, limited to 3 yearsRemuneration: Collective agreement of the state Hesse (TV-H) / E13The Senckenberg Society for Nature Research is a member of the Leibniz Association and has been investigating the “Earth System” worldwide for more than 200 years, examining the past, analysing the present, and developing projections for the future. We conduct integrative geobiodiversity research with the aim of understanding nature in all its complexity and diversity in order to preserve it as the foundation of life for future generations and to ensure its sustainable use. Across eight institutes and five research stations throughout Germany, scientists from more than 40 countries conduct research at the highest international level.The mission of the Senckenberg Biodiversity and Climate Research Centre is to study the complex interactions between biodiversity, climate and society.SBiK-F has strong cooperations with the Institute for social-ecological research (ISOE) and the position will work closely with both institutions.The position develops quantitative approaches to (1) better characterize and measure human–nature interactions, or (2) use these analyses to identify leverage points for more effective stewardship or monitoring of nature under climate change.Your tasks- Develop quantitative approaches to measure and analyze human–nature interactions- Integrate multiple data streams (ecological, social, remote-sensing, citizen-science) into coherent models of social-ecological system dynamics- Identify leverage points where intervention or monitoring most effectively supports biodiversity- Advance biodiversity or stewardship monitoring frameworks to better incorporate social dimensions- Publish in leading international journals- Contribute to and connect with ongoing research at SBiK-F- Collaborate across the natural- and social-science groups at Senckenberg, ISOE, and partner institutionsYour profile- PhD in ecology, environmental science, quantitative social science, or a related field- Demonstrated experience working with empirical ecological data and preferably also social data- Strong proficiency in R (and/or comparable statistical/programming environments)- Excellent quantitative and statistical skills- Strong publication record in international peer-reviewed journals- Fluency in written and spoken EnglishDesirable skills- Experience with integrating heterogeneous data streams (eg. ecological, social, remote sensing or citizen science data)- Familiarity with AI/ML methods- Track record of interdisciplinary collaboration across natural and social sciences- Experience in quantitative social science methods and working with social or socio-economic data- Experience in acquiring third-party funding- Familiarity with trait-based approaches to social-ecological questions- Familiarity with adaptive capacity and resilience of social-ecological systems- Familiarity with impacts of climate change on the interactions between biodiversity and societyWe offer- access to an international network of scientists, policymakers and research organizations- an attractive job within the inspired and dynamic working environment of an internationally recognized research institution- flexible working hours – mobile working options – employee ID card with free admission to Senckenberg museums – annual special payment – collectively agreed vacation entitlement – company pension planSenckenberg is committed to diversity. We benefit from the different expertise, perspectives and personalities of our staff and welcome every application from qualified candidates, irrespective of ethnic or cultural origin, age, gender, ethnic or cultural origin, religion or belief, age, sexual identity or and ideology, sexual orientation and identity or disability. Applicants with a severe disability will be given special consideration in case of equal suitability. Senckenberg actively supports the compatibility of work and family and places great emphasis on an equal and inclusive work culture.How to apply?Please upload your application (letter of motivation with a short description of your previous and current research foci, a CV with full publication list, copies of certificates and diplomas, along with the names of two referees), electronically (as a single PDF) stating the reference: #11-26026 by 29.11.2026.Please submit your application via our online application system. If you are viewing this vacancy on an external job platform, please visit our careers page and apply via the corresponding "Apply" button. Applications submitted by email cannot be considered.Please be aware, application documents will also be made available to members of the selection committee from the Institute for Social-Ecological Research (ISOE), solely for the purpose of assessing applications and selecting candidates.ContactSenckenberg Gesellschaft für NaturforschungSenckenberganlage 2560325 Frankfurt am MainFor specific questions about this role, please contact Prof. Dr. Thomas Müller atThomas Müller.For data protection information on the processing of personal data as part of the application and selection process, please refer to the privacy policy on our homepage at https://www.senckenberg.de/en/imprint/Please visit our website at www.senckenberg.de for further information about the Senckenberg Gesellschaft für Naturforschung.

In this role, you will lead platform‑level system engineering activities during Phase A/B1, orchestrate technical inputs from expert teams and subcontractors, and help define the mission and system architecture. You will contribute to laying the technical, programmatic, and schedule foundations that ensure mission success through the entire development lifecycle.Tasks:- Support the Lead System Engineer for the Phase A/B1 study.- Coordinate technical inputs from specialist engineering departments and individual subcontractors.- Execute trade‑offs and analyses to define the mission and system architecture.- Lead the parts of the platform and subsystem system design as an architect, including deriving and maintaining requirements from satellite to subsystem level.- Support Model-Based Systems Engineering (MBSE) activities for the mission.- Contribute to the assessment of the satellite development approach to ensure the target Technology Readiness Level (TRL) by the end of Phase B1.- Support the definition of the overall project breakdown structure (Work Breakdown Structure) for phases B2, C/D, and E1 through in‑orbit commissioning.- Assist in developing the programme plan for the satellite across phases B2, C/D, and E1 up to in‑orbit calibration and validation.- Support the creation of a project implementation schedule for the platform, aligned with the overall programme planning.Analyse and assess potential cost drivers for the platform.- Support the identification and evaluation of technical and programmatic risks, including cost, schedule, and feasibility drivers.- Support the definition and implementation of risk mitigation measures for the platform.Your QualificationsMinimum:- Master-level degree in aerospace engineering with a focus on space systems- Knowledge of science, exploration and space safety space missions- Competencies in space mission design, satellite systems engineering and spacecraft subsystem design- High level of flexibility, willingness to work in international teams and ability to keep tight schedules- High motivation, pro-active working approach and strong sense of responsibility- Excellent communication, presentation and documentation skills- Fluency in both spoken and written (business) EnglishIdeal:- Industry experience in space system engineering- Knowledge of requirements engineering for subsystems of space systems and preparation of specifications- Experience in Model Based Systems Engineering- Fluency in German language

jobs.occupation: PhD Candidate / Doctoral Researcher – Lipidomics and Fatty Acid Metabolism in Inflammation (Wissenschaftliche/r Mitarbeiter/in)
jobs.description: ...you're in the middle of itThe Institute of Clinical Pharmacology at Goethe University Frankfurt is seeking a PhD Candidate / Doctoral Researcher to join the research group of Dr. Hahnefeld. The successful candidate will contribute to an interdisciplinary research project in cooperation with the Fraunhofer ITMP Frankfurt at the interface of analytical chemistry, lipid biology and inflammation research.The project investigates how lipid metabolism and lipid-mediated signaling are regulated in inflammatory settings. The work combines cell-based experiments with mass spectrometry-based lipidomics, fatty acid analysis and targeted lipid mediator measurements. A particular focus will be placed on the development, optimization and application of robust analytical and computational workflows for the analysis of complex biological datasets. The research group uses high-resolution mass spectrometry and reproducible bioinformatic approaches to investigate lipid-mediated mechanisms in inflammatory and metabolic diseases. The position offers the opportunity to work in a collaborative research environment with interdisciplinary partners in lipid biology, immunology, imaging and proteomics.The position is limited up to three years.Your Role:- Plan, conduct and document experiments in cellular models of inflammation and metabolic perturbation.- Prepare biological samples and perform LC-HRMS-based lipidomics and metabolomics measurements and further develop associated analytical workflows.- Perform GC-HRMS-based analysis of fatty acids- Conduct LC-MS/MS measurements of lipid mediators using established methods.- Perform comprehensive quality control, raw-data validation, data annotation and statistical analysis of complex mass spectrometry datasets.- Develop and apply reproducible workflows for data processing, visualization and interpretation using R and/or Python.- Contribute to the integration and interpretation of lipidomics data with complementary datasets generated by collaborating groups, including imaging- and proteomics-based data.- Validate selected findings in close collaboration with project partners.- Present research results in scientific publications, project meetings and at national and international conferences.... your skills are what we're looking for- A completed Master’s degree or equivalent qualification in analytical chemistry, chemistry, pharmacy, biochemistry, molecular life sciences or a related discipline.- A strong theoretical and practical background in analytical chemistry.- Practical experience with liquid chromatography, gas chromatography and mass spectrometry is desirable.- Experience with high-resolution mass spectrometry, lipidomics, metabolomics, method development or biological sample preparation is advantageous but not necessary.- Experience in cell culture, molecular or cellular biology is advantageous.- Knowledge of statistical data analysis and programming in R and/or Python, or a strong willingness to acquire these skills.- A careful, structured and independent working style, combined with reliability and the ability to work effectively in an interdisciplinary team.- Very good written and spoken English skills.- Due to legal regulations, valid proof of measles immunity / measles vaccination is required... you'll be offered a lot- In addition to an attractive salary based on acollective agreement (TV-G-U, E 13)with an annual special payment, you benefit from long-term security through company pension schemes- An interdisciplinary doctoral research project at the interface of analytical chemistry, lipidomics and inflammation research.- Close scientific supervision and structured training in high-resolution mass spectrometry, lipidomics, fatty acid analysis and reproducible data analysis.- Remote Work possible- Benefit from our attractive health offers. We offer regular online and face-to-face courses on nutrition, relaxation, sports and exercise- Part-time employment is possible, we offer childcare in our daycare center (if you have any questions, please contact UKF-Familienservice), child care during holidays- Free public transport in all Hessen (Free State Ticket Hessen)- Uniklinik-Campus, Mensa, Cafés- Insights: Instagram, YouTube, LinkedIn- FAQ´s for new employees**It's time to join our team! **Contact: Dr. Lisa Hahnefeld, Leader Research GroupEmail: hahnefeld@med.uni-frankfurt.de** **Application Deadline: 08.11.2026We welcome applications from candidates of all genders. Women are currently underrepresented in these positions at Universitätsmedizin Frankfurt. Therefore, applications from women are especially encouraged. Applicants with severe disabilities will be given preferential consideration in cases of equal personal and professional qualifications.
